info.title: Sales Stock Integrator Sysnet API
info.description:
## Authorization
We use bearer auth throughout the API. Generally, API requests should have the follow header:  
{  
    "content-type": "application/json",  
    "Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN_GOES_HERE"  
}  
Please refer to the Auth section immediately below for details on getting your token.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to group results.
                        The fieldName can be any of the following: organisationId, taxNameId.
                        The sort could either have - to sort by descending and + to sort by ascending. See groupQuery schema for more info.
                        For grouping using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: groupSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise grouped results by aggregating the groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: venueRefId, taxNameId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: totalSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise all grouped results by aggregating all the groups sub groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: venueRefId, taxNameId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: searchDistinct
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to get the distinct values for a field. 
                Only the field specified will be returned in the results. This can be used with filtering functionality, sort and limit. 
                However it cannot be used with group, groupSummary or totalSummary.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to change the sorting of results returned. 
                        The default sort is venueId ascending. 
                        Use any fieldNames comma separated in the sort. 
                        Use + for ascending - for descending 
                        eg +updateDateTime.
                        - venueId would sort by updateDateTime ascending and then venueId descending.
 For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name
                        For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: This limits the amount of results returned. This default limit Is set to 20. The maximum limit is 200.

parameters.name: registrationCode
parameters.description:
Corresponds to the Sysnet Registration Number for the Venue Example Value: 1234
This parameter searches for the registrationCode field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: venueName
parameters.description:
Example Value: Brads Burger House
This parameter searches for the venueName field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: venueRefId
parameters.description: integer: This parameter searches the venueRefId field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all venueRefIds greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for venueRefIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg venueRefId=>5& venueRefId=<10 would search for all venueRefIds between 5 and 10.

This header will be returned with the total available results for a query. 
                              This may be different from the current number of results returned.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: This parameter is used to change the default offset from 0. Offset is the position in the dataset of a particular record. By specifying offset, you retrieve a subset of records starting with the offset value. Eg: If you have 100 records in your result set, and you want to retrieve records 50 to 80, you will need to use offset=49 and limit = 30.

rid_chain.name: rid_chain
rid_chain.description: The rid_chain is used to track the current users session. It should be a unique value that identifies a users particular session in a particular device. When events are received through H&L websocket events, the current user's session can be identified with this value. As such this value can help you determine which device a user was on when they made a request on this API.

search.name: search
search.description:
This does an advanced search using a url encoded JSON object.

Most fields available in the return object can be searched using this methodology.
Example: search={ "status": "active"} would search the status field for the value: 'active'.

Searching is also possible using nested fields. Use the following syntax: <object>.<field> to specify the nested field.
Example: search={ "Stock.name": "Best Beer" }

There are a couple of extra operators that can be used in the search. These are $or, $and, $not.
Example: search={ "$or": [ { "status": "bad" }, { "status": "worse" } ] }. Searches for the statuses of 'bad' or 'worse'.
The $or, $and and $not operators can be nested.

If the name pair contains a fieldName it is possible for the value to be a sub-object containing any number of operators. The operators depend on the fieldType of the fieldName:

Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }

Relative Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }
This 'relativeDateTime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time

Number Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $between, $notBetween, $in, $notIn
Example: search={ "totalCount": { "$gt": 10 } }

String Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $in, $like, $iLike, $notLike, $notILike, $notIn
Example: search={ "failReason": { "$in": ["Out of bounds", "Out of time"] } }

These operators equate to Sequelize operators. See Operators | Sequelize
